text.free_hand: Free a hand to turn the fixed indexing selector.
text.howto_turn: Use a free hand at the mounted left selector to step forward or back through sixteen indexed pantograph configurations. O is the fixed pale origin. Four original rigid bars form the extended parallelogram: blue OB and gold BE are360 millimetres long, green AD and violet DC are180 millimetres. Each bar keeps its original webs, bosses and vertices. Five genuinely hollow receiver bores surround continuous original axles and retaining heads. Pale D is the tracer head at the short-bar joint; orange E is the marker at the far end of the extended gold bar. In ideal mechanism XY coordinates about O, A=L*u, B=2L*u, D=L*(u+v), C=2L*u+L*v and E=2D, with L180 millimetres. The two direction vectors use alpha=40+20cos(theta) and beta=140+20sin(theta) degrees, theta22.5 degrees per phase. Supported millidegree rotation and integer translation tables introduce small measured joint and marker-coordinate tolerances while retaining positive full-depth bore and head clearances. All four original bars and both markers restore after the closed sixteen-pose path, without scaling, per-endpoint correction, replacement or reset. This physical linkage has two degrees of freedom; the selector chooses a predefined sampled two-angle configuration path, not a physical one-crank drive or arbitrary user tracing. Blue and orange fixed backing dots are mathematical marker-coordinate references at another depth, so neither pixel coincidence nor a perspective image ratio is promised. Inspect the assembled layered joints from an oblique view. This indexed geometric exhibit creates no pen contact, drawing or line, physical force, friction or power transmission, continuous constraint or swept collision simulation, portable output or loose-item custody.
